conclusion.canonical: For every finite ordinary tree T with integer p=alpha(T)-2 and x(T)+2<=p, the complete sum over original leaves v satisfying Delta_p(T-v)<0 of Delta_(p-1)(T-{v,s_v})-Delta_(p-1)(T-N_T[s_v]) is nonpositive.
clauses: For every finite ordinary tree T with integer p=alpha(T)-2 and x(T)+2<=p, the complete sum over original leaves v satisfying Delta_p(T-v)<0 of Delta_(p-1)(T-{v,s_v})-Delta_(p-1)(T-N_T[s_v]) is nonpositive.

definitions.canonical: Maximum cardinality of an independent vertex set in the finite graph.
definitions.name: def-alpha

definitions.canonical: An original vertex has exactly one adjacent vertex, not an isolate.
definitions.name: def-leaf

definitions.canonical: Unique original neighbor of a leaf; arbitrary off the leaf set.
definitions.name: def-support

definitions.canonical: Natural count of independent k-subsets of the original carrier avoiding deletion set D, including zero counts above capacity.
definitions.name: def-count

definitions.canonical: Integer difference i_(k+1)(G-D)-i_k(G-D). The intended integer coefficients are zero outside feasible ranks.
definitions.name: def-delta

definitions.canonical: Least natural index with strict negative full-graph forward difference, defined by Nat.find; terminal zero extension proves existence.
definitions.name: def-crossing

definitions.canonical: Deletion set {v,s_v} using the original leaf support.
definitions.name: def-h

definitions.canonical: Original closed neighborhood of s_v as a deletion set.
definitions.name: def-r

definitions.canonical: Strict negativity of the vertex-deleted difference at the original rank p; its independent-set count is the original-carrier avoiding-{v} representation.
definitions.name: def-favorable

definitions.canonical: Integer sum over every favorable original leaf vertex, retaining shared-support multiplicity, of forwardDifferenceDel(H,p-1)-forwardDifferenceDel(R,p-1).
definitions.name: def-aggregate

hypotheses.canonical: G is connected and acyclic, exactly an ordinary finite tree.

With integer p=alpha(G)-2, x(G)+2<=p. The exact Lean Nat premise is equivalent: it forces alpha>=4 and p>=2, so both subtractions in the aggregate agree with integer ranks. Alpha>=7 is a conclusion to prove, not an added premise.

lean_binding.lean_statement:
theorem firstInteriorAggregate {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hT : G.IsTree)
    (hInterior : C5LA1.crossingIndex G + 2 ≤ G.indepNum - 2) :
    C5LA1.aggregate G (G.indepNum - 2) ≤ 0
